title: RWB-E1-013: DP-17 removes the data lake while the two criteria this service owns assert the INT-19 extract, its trailer and the lake hold
source: Template and Rules v1 R5.5 (DP-17), R7.2 and R9; WP B2-P9-001 story lines RWB-P9-E1013-APP, RWB-P9-E1013-CON and RWB-P9-E1013-OPS; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 8, 9 and 37; FSD P9 Reporting v3 A2.1.2 and A2.1.4; TSD P9 Reporting v2 T5.1 and T5.3; legacy RWB-E1-013 sections 2, 3, 4, 7, 8, 12, 14, 17 and 19
section: Sections 2, 4, 5, 7, 8, 12.3, 14, 17 and 19 of the APP and CON stories; sections 3, 5, 7, 12.3 and 19 of the OPS story
description: Legacy AC3 asserts that the INT-19 extract for a business date is in the data lake with its freshness stamp and its row count in the trailer, and legacy AC7 asserts that the extract is held when the lake load area does not answer, with MSG-GEN-006 naming Data lake. Both criteria are owned by RWB-P9-E1013-APP under this WP. Arch v5 removes the data lake, INT-19 and INT-20 and states that the data lake and Power BI are not connected (DP-17, ADR-018), so no target system receives the extract and no target component can be unavailable in the way AC7 describes. The legacy text is kept word for word as the record of intent, and the deliverable proved instead is the publish state of measure_publish with its hold reason and freshness stamp inside rwb_reporting.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E1-013 AC3 and AC7, message MSG-GEN-006 and business rule BR5; Template and Rules v1 R5.5 row DP-17 (Removed; no data lake; gap if the story needs lake data); Architecture v5 slide 8 (Data lake / Power BI: not connected, INT-19 and INT-20 removed) and slide 9 (the Airflow notes name report extracts, with no destination); TSD P9 T5.1 (INT-19 Data lake and Power BI, daily batch)
legacy_ref: RWB-E1-013 (AC3, AC7, BR5, X4, MSG-GEN-006, section 19)
proposed: Keep the legacy criteria word for word, prove the publish, the freshness stamp, the hold and the resend on measure_publish inside rwb_reporting, declare no lake path and no extract element in the contract, and let a later decision register decide whether a reporting extract to any destination is rebuilt

title: RWB-E1-013: the plan's C row names two rwb-case contracts and omits the two rwb-source-data rows the run consumes
source: Template and Rules v1 R5.4 (dependency classes) and R9; WP B2-P9-001 story lines (C row of RWB-P9-E1013-APP and of RWB-P9-E1013-CON); FSD P9 Reporting v3 A2.1.2; TSD P9 Reporting v2 T5.1, T5.2 and T-A; Architecture v5 slide 13 (P9 Reporting: E to P3, P6, S2, S3, S6, S7 and P8; T to P2; R and S to P1); legacy RWB-E1-013 section 12
section: Metadata (Contract dependencies); sections 3, 4, 7, 12.2, 12.5 and 13 of the APP story; sections 2, 3, 12.2 and 13 of the CON story
description: The run of JOB-15 reads the payments since entry and the daily completeness gate, and both are rows of rwb-source-data in the target: the payments read and the freshness answer. The plan gives this key contract dependencies of RWB-P3-E1043-CON and RWB-P3-E1018-CON only, so two class C rows are consumed in fact and absent from the metadata, and the two activities RWB-P1-E1013-APP registers for a measures consumer are named in no row either. The story keeps the metadata exactly as the plan states it and declares the two rows as class C in 12.2 with their fakes.
evidence: WP B2-P9-001 story line RWB-P9-E1013-APP with C of two P3 rows; legacy section 12 Published interfaces (RecoveryDataApi.paymentsSinceEntry and DailyCompletenessGate.check, both owned elsewhere); FSD P9 A2.1.2 Integration points (Power BI, Data lake); TSD P9 T5.1 (INT-19) and T5.2; Architecture v5 slide 13 row P9 Reporting (T to P2, S and R to P1)
proposed: Keep the metadata rows as the plan states them, declare the payments and freshness rows plus the two rwb-case rows as consumed in 12.2 with their fakes, and add the two rwb-source-data rows to the dependency map of the wave

title: RWB-E1-013: the definition load of table measure_definition has no target operation, because the table is P9's while the reference-load framework is rwb-case's
source: Template and Rules v1 R3 (default rulings), R5.5 (DP-07) and R9; WP B2-P9-001 story lines RWB-P9-E1013-APP and RWB-P9-E1013-CON; FSD P9 Reporting v3 A2.1.2 and A2.1.3.1; TSD P9 Reporting v2 T3.1 and T-A; legacy RWB-E1-013 sections 4, 7 (AC1, AC4), 12, 13 and 16 (TC-E1-013-09); RWB-P3-E1013-APP section 12
section: Sections 3, 4, 7, 12.1, 13 and 19 of the APP story; sections 4, 7, 12.1 and 19 of the CON story
description: Legacy AC1 and AC4 load the definition file through POST /admin/reference-loads with table measure_definition, an operation of the reference-data framework, and legacy TC-E1-013-09 tests a refusal on that path. In the target the reference-data framework and its lists belong to rwb-case (DP-07, RWB-PLT-E1043-CON, RWB-P3-E1043-CON), while measure_definition is P9's own table in rwb_reporting (Ownership Map), so the load cannot run on the rwb-case path and no source gives the P9 path, its element or its right. The CON declares the reference-load element of the table with the placeholder and the APP keeps the legacy value of the approver and the all-or-nothing rule.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E1-013 section 4 step 1 (POST /admin/reference-loads with table measure_definition), AC1, AC4 and TC-E1-013-09; Template and Rules v1 R3 default ruling (reference data owner P3 rwb-case) and R5.5 row DP-07; TSD P9 T3.1 (measure_definition, source Workbench) and T-A.1 (one operation only); RWB-P3-E1013-APP section 12 (the definition load is refused with MSG-P4-002 on the rwb-case path)
proposed: Declare the reference-load element of table measure_definition on the rwb-reporting base, keep the list values on the rwb-case reference-data contract, and let the owner of rwb-case confirm whether the load of a P9 table belongs to the framework or to this service

title: RWB-E1-013: the Ownership Map gives rwb-reporting no event while the wave 1 harness names rwb.reporting.ReportPublished.v1 on the service topic
source: Template and Rules v1 R4 and R9; WP B2-P9-001 story lines RWB-P9-E1013-APP, RWB-P9-E1013-CON and RWB-P9-E1013-OPS; context pack P9 (Events (0), topic rwb.reporting.events.v1); RWB-ITG-E1013-ITG sections 12 and 18
section: Metadata (Patterns applied); sections 12.3, 12.4 and 19 of the APP and CON stories; sections 12.3 and 19 of the OPS story
description: The context pack and the Ownership Map give rwb-reporting the topic rwb.reporting.events.v1 and the retry and .dlt topics by the naming rule, and no event row. RWB-ITG-E1013-ITG declares rwb.reporting.ReportPublished.v1 on that topic as the freshness signal of its journey and cites this story as the publisher. A service that publishes from an outbox would also need the DP-09 library row RWB-PLT-TE006-CON, which is in no pattern set of this key. The three stories of this WP therefore declare 12.3 and 12.4 as None and record the conflict rather than inventing an event contract.
evidence: Context pack P9 '## Ownership rows owned by P9 / ### Events (0) - None'; Template and Rules v1 R4 (topic per service) and R5.5 DP-09 (H RWB-PLT-TE006-CON); RWB-ITG-E1013-ITG fragment events_consumed (rwb.reporting.ReportPublished.v1) and its ADR-015 row
proposed: Declare no event in these three stories, keep the topic provisioned by the platform, and let the owner of the reporting read model decide whether a freshness event is published and, if it is, raise it as its own story with the outbox library row

title: RWB-E1-013: the Power BI refresh that AC3 asserts has no mechanism once the data lake is removed, and the measures read is assigned to Epic 2 by the legacy story
source: Template and Rules v1 R5.5 (DP-17) and R9; WP B2-P9-001 story lines RWB-P9-E1013-APP and RWB-P9-E1013-CON; FSD P9 Reporting v3 A2.1.2, A2.1.4.2 and A2.3; TSD P9 Reporting v2 T-A.1 and T-A.2; Architecture v5 slides 8, 9 and 37; legacy RWB-E1-013 AC3, sections 12, 13 and 19
section: Sections 2, 4, 12.1, 12.9 and 19 of the APP story; sections 2, 12.1 and 19 of the CON story
description: The legacy story says that the Power BI data set refreshes at 07:30 from the extract, and it also says that no endpoint exists in Epic 1 and that GET /reports/measures reads the snapshot from RWB-E2-009. Arch v5 removes the lake and does not connect Power BI, so no source says how the report reaches the snapshot in the target. The Ownership Map nevertheless gives the measures operation to P9, and the wave 1 harness calls it. The CON declares the shape of the operation so that the harness and the P3 catalog can build on Day 1, and the dashboard, its filters and SCR-37 stay RWB-P9-E2009-APP's.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E1-013 section 4 step 8 (07:30 refresh from the extract), section 12 (No endpoint in Epic 1) and section 19; FSD P9 A2.8.4.1 (the operation and the 07:30 refresh); TSD P9 T-A.1 (API-P9-001, first in E2); Architecture v5 slide 8 (Data lake / Power BI: not connected); context pack P9 (REST operations provided: GET /reports/measures)
proposed: Declare the measures read in the wave 1 contract for the harness and the catalog consumer, keep the dashboard and its data set in RWB-P9-E2009-APP, and leave the connection of any reporting client to the read as an open decision for the PRD step

title: RWB-E1-013: the approver of a definition is typed uuid by the TSD while the legacy criteria and the FSD name the reference TRB-0001
source: Template and Rules v1 R3 (precedence) and R9; WP B2-P9-001 story lines RWB-P9-E1013-APP and RWB-P9-E1013-CON; FSD P9 Reporting v3 A2.1.4.1 and A2.3.3.2; TSD P9 Reporting v2 T3.1; legacy RWB-E1-013 AC1 and section 11
section: Sections 3, 7, 11 and 14 of the APP story; sections 5, 7 and 11 of the CON story
description: TSD P9 T3.1 types measure_definition.approved_by as uuid and approved_at as timestamptz, while legacy AC1 and the FSD field catalogue name the approver as the reference TRB-0001 with an approval date. A reference is not a uuid, so either the column carries a user identity or the legacy value is a display reference of the approver row. Neither source resolves it, and no value may be invented, so the CON declares the TSD type and carries TRB-0001 as a comment on the element, and the APP keeps both legacy values verbatim in AC1.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E1-013 AC1 ('approver "TRB-0001" with approval date 2026-11-20') and section 11 (DF-RPT-038 approved_by, DF-RPT-039 approved_at); FSD P9 A2.3.3.2 (measure_definition.approved_by, uuid, No, None); TSD P9 T3.1 (DF-RPT-038 approved_by USER_REF uuid)
proposed: Declare approved_by uuid as the TSD types it, carry the legacy reference TRB-0001 as a comment and a test fixture, and let the owner of the role model confirm which reference a definition row stores

title: RWB-E1-013: no source gives the path or the shape of the definitions read that RWB-P3-E1013-APP consumes across the service boundary
source: Template and Rules v1 R5.5 (DP-11) and R9; WP B2-P9-001 story line RWB-P9-E1013-CON; TSD P9 Reporting v2 T-A.1 and T-A.2; legacy RWB-E1-013 section 12 (MeasureCatalog); RWB-P3-E1013-APP sections 3, 12.2 and 12.8
section: Sections 4, 12.1, 12.8 and 19 of the APP story; sections 1, 4, 7, 12.1 and 12.8 of the CON story
description: The legacy story offers MeasureCatalog as a Java interface and offers no endpoint, and the TSD endpoint inventory holds API-P9-001 only. RWB-P3-E1013-APP consumes the definitions in force on a date to refuse a band-list version that retires a band a definition still uses, and it names the operation without a path. The CON therefore declares GET /measure-definitions with the query parameter onDate and a definition list answer, and marks the path and the field list as a target declaration pending the P3 team's confirmation.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E1-013 section 12 Published interfaces (MeasureCatalog.inForce(LocalDate)); TSD P9 T-A.1 (one operation, API-P9-001); RWB-P3-E1013-APP section 3 and section 12.2 (the catalog read, path not specified in the source documents); RWB-P3-E1013-APP fragment ops_consumed (GET /api/recovery/reporting/v1/measure-definitions?onDate={date})
proposed: Declare the definitions read on the reporting base with onDate and the definition element, fake it for the P3 story, and confirm the path and the field list in the baseline review of this contract

title: RWB-E1-013: JOB-15 has two candidate triggers, the Temporal Schedule of DP-10 and the Airflow chain that triggers report extracts
source: Template and Rules v1 R5.5 (DP-10) and R9; WP B2-P9-001 story lines RWB-P9-E1013-APP and RWB-P9-E1013-OPS; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 9 (Airflow notes) and slide 5 (batch role); TSD P9 Reporting v2 T1 and appendix T-B (DL06); legacy RWB-E1-013 section 12 (Quartz, nightly 01:30)
section: Sections 4, 12.6 and 19 of the APP story; sections 4, 5, 7, 12.6 and 19 of the OPS story; section 12.6 of the CON story
description: Arch v5 slide 9 describes the bank's Airflow as the scheduler that opens the ACE chain, waits for the daily case run, opens the file windows and triggers report extracts in rwb-reporting, while DP-10 replaces the Quartz row of JOB-nn with a Temporal Schedule in the owning service and the legacy job runs nightly at 01:30. Two triggers for one run would publish a business date twice or leave it to whichever arrives first. This WP registers one Schedule, at 01:30 Asia/Bangkok, and records that no Airflow call is wired to the run.
evidence: Architecture v5 slide 9 notes ('It triggers report extracts in rwb-reporting', with the scheduler outside the cluster) and slide 5 (the batch role kept as the bank's Airflow); Template and Rules v1 R5.5 row DP-10; legacy RWB-E1-013 section 12 (Trigger: Quartz, nightly 01:30 Asia/Bangkok); TSD P9 appendix T-B DL06
proposed: Register the one Schedule at 01:30 and leave the Airflow call of a report extract unwired, and settle in the batch and scheduling work whether any extract trigger returns and what it calls

title: RWB-E1-013: the alert thresholds, the channel names and the run-book identifiers of JOB-15 have no source, and MSG-GEN-006 loses its caller with the lake
source: Template and Rules v1 R9; WP B2-P9-001 story line RWB-P9-E1013-OPS; TSD P9 Reporting v2 T7 (NFR-067, NFR-068); FSD P9 Reporting v3 A2.1.3.1; legacy RWB-E1-013 section 14 (MSG-GEN-006)
section: Sections 3, 4, 5, 8, 13 and 14 of the OPS story
description: NFR-067 and NFR-068 require monitoring, a run book and an alert to a named owner within a target, and neither the FSD, the TSD nor the legacy story gives an alert threshold, a channel name, a run-book path or the expected minutes of JOB-15. MSG-GEN-006 is defined for an unavailable data lake, and with the lake removed the message has no system to name unless the held publish adopts it. The OPS story reads every threshold, channel and owner from the catalogue row and the values files, and names the held publish as the one caller of MSG-GEN-006.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E1-013 section 14 (MSG-GEN-006 {system} is not available) and section 13 (feature flag only); FSD P9 A2.1.3.1 (VR-P9-001-1 with MSG-P1-001, no threshold); TSD P9 T7 (NFR-067 'Every scheduled job has a run book, monitoring and an alert'; NFR-068 'within its target')
proposed: Keep every threshold, channel and owner as a catalogue or values-file entry, take the 15-minute failed-run target from NFR-068, and have the operations owner name the caller of MSG-GEN-006 in the run book rather than in code

title: RWB-E1-013: the three measure tables' DDL sits with no DB story of this key, so the app story's migration carries it
source: Template and Rules v1 R5.5 (DP-15), R5.7 (Day-1 rules) and R9; WP B2-P9-001 story lines RWB-P9-E1013-APP and RWB-P9-E1013-OPS; TSD P9 Reporting v2 T3.1; legacy RWB-E1-013 section 13 (V1_013__measures.sql)
section: Sections 3, 11 and 13 of the APP story; sections 3, 11 and 13 of the OPS story
description: The legacy story owns both tables and its migration V1_013__measures.sql. The story set of this WP holds an app, a contract and a deployment story and no DB story, so no row of the key carries the DDL, while DP-15 gives every service its own Flyway sequence and the deployment story must run a migration before the release is ready. The app story therefore carries the three tables, their unique keys and the frozen-row trigger in V1013__measures.sql and the deployment story replays the same sequence, and the assignment is recorded rather than left to the build.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E1-013 section 13 (Database: new tables measure_definition and measure_snapshot, Flyway migration V1_013__measures.sql); TSD P9 T3.1 (measure_definition, measure_snapshot and measure_publish, all NEW); Template and Rules v1 R5.5 row DP-15; WP B2-P9-001 story lines with no DB work type; context pack P9 (Tables (3))
proposed: Carry the three tables and the frozen-row trigger in the app story's V1013__measures.sql in the per-service sequence, replay the same sequence in the deployment story, and raise a DB story of this service only if the template requires the DDL in one owner
